sources.entry: apiflask - A lightweight Python web API framework based on Flask, supporting marshmallow schemas and Pydantic models.

summary.one_liner: APIFlask is a lightweight Python web API framework built on Flask that adds decorator-based input/output handling, automatic validation, and auto-generated OpenAPI docs, supporting both marshmallow schemas and Pydantic models.
summary.what_it_does: APIFlask extends Flask with an APIFlask application class and an APIBlueprint class, so you use it in place of Flask's own objects while keeping the rest of the Flask API. It adds decorators such as @app.input(), @app.output(), and route shortcuts like @app.get() and @app.post() to declare request parsing and response formatting for view functions. Request data is validated and deserialized automatically, and return values are serialized to JSON, with support for both marshmallow schemas and Pydantic models through a pluggable schema adapter system. It generates an OpenAPI Specification document, available at a URL and via the flask spec command, and serves interactive docs using Swagger UI by default or other UIs such as Redoc, Elements, RapiDoc, and RapiPDF. The abort() helper returns JSON error responses, and the README also mentions Flask-HTTPAuth integration for authentication and async def view support.
use_cases: building a JSON REST API in Python
validating incoming request bodies with schemas
generating OpenAPI docs for a Flask app
adding interactive API docs to a Flask backend
migrating a Flask app to typed request/response handling
using Pydantic models for API validation
how_to_run: Save the example code as app.py
flask spec (to print the OpenAPI spec)
notable: Pluggable schema adapter system that supports both marshmallow schemas and Pydantic models
Automatic OpenAPI document generation plus several selectable docs UIs via docs_ui
Designed as a thin wrapper: code written for Flask generally still works, per the README
Async view support via async def (optional async extra)
caveats: Pydantic support is shown in the README only as an alternative; marshmallow is the primary example style
The README does not describe deployment or production hardening
